messages:
maria (storage): heads-up — eu-west2 scratch pool is trending to 92% wear for a subset of drives, provisioning queue is backing up GPU allocs :grimacing:
kevin (infra): ugh. seen anything that spikes iops or is this steady wear? :eyes:
maria (storage): steady increase over last 48h, but correlates with a large batch of rnns + long seqs. scrub backlog also up. hitting our "urgent-replace" threshold in the telemetry. snippet:```drive_group=eu-west2-scratch
p99_iops=21k
avg_write_rate=430MB/s
wear_percentiles=[70,88,92]
scrub_pending=28k_files
pending_gpu_allocs=12
```
alex (sre): how much of that 12 blocked allocs are high-priority prod vs canary?
tanya (prod): 8 prod (latency-sensitive), 4 canary. Prod queue is flapping auto-scale, saw 20% failed launches last 30m.
kevin (infra): immediate options: divert new low-priority allocations to us-west1, throttle long-seq jobs, or temporarily lower scrub concurrency. each has tradeoffs: region shift increases cross-region egress and latency; lowering scrub risks higher corruption window.
maria (storage): agree. I ran a quick sim — reducing scrub concurrency by 30% buys ~3h of headroom but increases probability of stale metadata during node restart by ~0.8%.
alex (sre): acceptable short-term if we put stricter canary gating. maybe implement a 2h window where we divert non-prod and reduce scrub.
tanya (prod): thumbs up from product side if we only divert non-prod. Prod teams prefer retries over cross-region latency.
kevin (infra): action plan proposal: 1) divert non-prod GPU allocs from eu-west2 -> us-west1 2) reduce scrub concurrency on drive_group=eu-west2-scratch by 30% 3) pin a temporary allocation quota to limit new long-seq jobs 4) open replacement ticket for top 5 drives hitting urgent threshold
maria (storage): implementing 1 and 2 now. patch I pushed:```bash
# scale down scrub workers
scrubctl set-concurrency --group eu-west2-scratch --percent 70
# update allocation filters
allocctl set-filter --region eu-west2 --allow prod-only
```
scrub-bot: scheduled: scrubctl job 4823 set-concurrency=70 for eu-west2-scratch at 2025-10-21T14:12Z :white_check_mark:
kevin (infra): doing 3) now — applying temporary quota via fleet controller.
tanya (prod): can you prod the canary gating? want to be sure nothing slips.
alex (sre): watching allocation logs. if failure rate drops under 5% in 15m we can extend the window. current error spike at 18% and falling.
maria (storage): also enabling extended KV cache retention for affected models to reduce read amplification:```feature-flag: kv-cache-extend=true --group eu-west2-scratch```
kevin (infra): cost note: diverting to us-west1 will add ~0.6c/token for the affected flows (rough estimate), and we'll burn modest egress credits. filing a cost impact note.
tanya (prod): okay to proceed. please tag any customer-facing incidents if latency > 150ms above baseline.
maria (storage): replacement ticket created: TICKET-4521, replacing 5 drives next maintenance window (48h SLA for hardware swap).
alex (sre): after 30m: failed launch rate down to 6%. maybe extend scrub reduction another 30m.
kevin (infra): extending 30m. leaving allocation filter for non-prod until we confirm drive replacements scheduled.
maria (storage): logging this as a wear-calibration event in postmortem tracker. will add this data point to wear forecasting model to suggest earlier rotation for similar seq-heavy workloads.
tanya (prod): thanks team. follow-up: can we get a quick doc on how to avoid hot-write patterns for long-seq workloads? I'll coordinate with ML infra.
maria (storage): will draft a short guide and share in #devex. :memo:
scrub-bot: note: scrub backlog reduced to 18k_files after concurrency change (30m).
alex (sre): resolving immediate alert if everyone agrees.
kevin (infra): agree. I'll keep the allocation filter until replacements complete. :thumbsup:
